concepts.def: The smallest particle of an element that can exist.
A substance made of only one type of atom.
Two or more elements chemically bonded in fixed proportions.
Substances together but not chemically bonded; separable physically.
Two or more atoms chemically bonded together.
Shows the elements and number of atoms in a substance, e.g. H₂O.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Atoms, Elements & Compounds — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Atoms, Elements & Compounds brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Atoms, Elements & Compounds.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

What does a curly arrow in an organic mechanism represent?

A curly arrow shows the movement of an atom from one position to another.
A curly arrow shows the direction in which heat is flowing in the reaction.

mcqs.q: Why is the hydration enthalpy of a small, highly charged ion very exothermic?
options: Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
Hydration enthalpy only depends on the size of the ion, not its charge.
Small/highly charged ions form strong ion-dipole attractions with water molecules, releasing a large amount of energy.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.

mcqs.q: If 50 cm^3 of a 1 mol/dm^3 solution is diluted to 100 cm^3, what is the new concentration?
options: The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
0.5 mol/dm^3 — the moles stay the same but the volume doubled.
The new concentration is 0.05 mol/dm^3 because you doubled the volume so you halve the concentration once and shift the decimal too.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ion”?
options: Average mass of atoms of an element compared to 1/12 the mass of a C-12 atom.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Smallest unit of an element; consists of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.
Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atom”?
options: Number of protons in the nucleus; defines the element.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Smallest unit of an element; consists of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.
Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Electron configuration”?
options: Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.
Smallest unit of an element; consists of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.
Average mass of atoms of an element compared to 1/12 the mass of a C-12 atom.
Arrangement of electrons in shells: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mass number”?
options: Average mass of atoms of an element compared to 1/12 the mass of a C-12 atom.
Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.
Arrangement of electrons in shells: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Relative atomic mass”?
options: Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Average mass of atoms of an element compared to 1/12 the mass of a C-12 atom.
Number of protons in the nucleus; defines the element.
Smallest unit of an element; consists of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atomic number”?
options: Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.
Number of protons in the nucleus; defines the element.
Smallest unit of an element; consists of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.

mcqs.q: How many neutrons in an atom with mass number 23 and atomic number 11?
options: 11 neutrons
14 neutrons
10 neutrons
12 neutrons
